negative_observations: At the native XML layer a custom StyleItem reference is lexically indistinguishable from a standard built-in style reference (both style:<Name> -> auto-prefixed d8p1:<Name>).

Internally, however, a custom StyleItem reference resolves to a raw '0:<uuid>' value (the StyleItem's own uuid attribute), unlike a standard built-in style reference which stays a named lexical form internally (see sibling S1 draft manifest) -- this is a genuine, previously-only-hypothesized (via unit tests) platform behavior now confirmed by real bytes.

The pre-VM cross-evidence-derived prediction for ChildObjects order (ascending class_id within CONFIGURATION_SECTION_1, i.e. StyleItem before Language) was WRONG; the real platform emits Language before StyleItem. No new InternalInfo entry was needed either way (confirmed correct).
non_claims: No claim about StyleItem Kind values other than Color (Font, Border are explicitly out of scope per the design's non-claims).
No claim about multiple StyleItem references, or StyleItem references outside a single AreaTemplate appearance context.
No claim that the observed ChildObjects order generalizes beyond this exact 3-child cohort (Language + StyleItem + Report); the ordering rule itself is not derived, only this one observed instance.
